items.text: Emma Allen, a British artist from London, took over 750 photographs after changing her face paint each time. She then created a stop-motion animation from the pictures, i.e. showing the pictures in a video at high speed to give the impression of movement. The artwork called Ruby is about rebirth and the transfer of energy, and it took Emma five days to create, working 17 hours a day. Difficult words: impression (feeling). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A British artist created an animation. She painted her face and took a picture of it. She repeated this process over 750 times. She changed her face paint a little each time. The pictures were then played at high speed. The artist worked 17 hours a day for five days to create the piece. The artwork is called Ruby and it is about rebirth and the transfer of energy. Difficult words: rebirth (when something becomes alive again after dying). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An artist makes an animation. She is from Britain. She paints her face and takes a photograph of it. Then she paints her face again. The second picture on her face is a little bit different. She takes a photograph again. She does this 750 times. She works 17 hours a day for five days. The pictures are put together. They are played fast. It looks like a movie. The animation is very interesting. It is about rebirth and transfer of energy. Difficult words: artist (somebody who produces art), rebirth (when something starts to live again), transfer (moving). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

As the fight for stricter gun laws in the United States continues after the latest school tragedy, an Alabama security company creates bulletproof safe rooms that will protect children from the terror of school shootings. Nationwide calls for stricter gun control laws haven’t been effective, and companies aren’t waiting for lawmakers. KT Solutions has developed a collapsible bulletproof shelter that can be installed inside classrooms. Kevin Thomas came up with the design after last year’s shooting in a school in Uvalde, Texas. The rapid-deploy safe room is set up in the corner of a classroom in as few as 10 seconds and it can be expanded. One shelter costs more than 50,000 dollars and it provides shelter against bullets in an active-shooter situation. According to Gun Violence Archive, there have been more mass shootings than days so far this year. Despite the innovations, Thomas says that his design isn’t a permanent solution to the gun epidemic in the US and that it’s necessary to fix the problem rather than its symptoms. Difficult words: collapsible (an object that can be folded into a small space), bulletproof (designed to resist bullets going through), permanent (lasting for a long time or forever). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in the US continue to fight for stricter gun laws, but lawmakers haven’t implemented any legislation yet. According to officials, this year, there were more mass shootings than days. A security company in Alabama developed bulletproof safe rooms which can protect children during such incidents. KT Solutions created a collapsible bulletproof room which workers install inside classrooms. It is possible to set up the room in 10 seconds and it protects children and teachers in situations when there’s a shooter in the school. Each room costs more than 50,000 dollars. Kevin Thomas is the designer of the rooms. He said that bulletproof rooms wouldn’t solve the problem of mass shootings, but they kept children safe if something like that happened. Difficult words: implement (to make a rule or law effective), bulletproof (safe from damage by shooting), collapsible (something which you can fold into a small space). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the United States, there are many mass shootings . This year, there are already more mass shootings than days. They happen in schools, too. It is necessary to protect children and teachers. But lawmakers work slowly. A security company in Alabama creates a safe room. This room stops bullets. People can put it up quickly in the corner of a classroom. One room costs over 50,000 dollars. Children and teachers can go inside if there is a shooter in a school. Kevin Thomas designs the room. He says that it is important to stop mass shootings rather than protect people when it happens. Difficult words: mass shooting (an incident when a person kills more people with a gun at one time), protect (to keep safe), lawmaker (a person who makes rules of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A sailor in England was trying to tie up his boat when he accidentally knocked the throttle and was thrown overboard. He had already unclipped the kill cord and pushed the throttle lever to full power, as he fell into the water. The six-meter-long speedboat began to circle the quay . Luckily though, a member of the public spotted it and raised alarm. A lifeboat crew managed to get a line aboard the spinning boat, reach the throttle lever, and reduce the speed. The boat’s owner managed to get ashore safely and was rushed to the hospital. Difficult words: throttle (a mechanism which controls the speed of something), kill cord (a line which connects a man and a boat and turns off the boat if the man falls out), quay (a place for boats to stop). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A sailor was trying to tie up his boat when he accidentally knocked the throttle . The boat started moving and threw the man overboard. The six-meter-long speedboat began to move in a circle. Luckily, somebody spotted the boat and let others know. The lifeboat crew got a line aboard the boat and managed to reduce the speed. The owner of the boat got safely to shore, but he had to go to the hospital. Difficult words: throttle (a mechanism which controls the speed), spot (see), lifeboat crew (people who help sailors). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man is on a boat. He wants to tie up the boat. Something happens. He moves the throttle by accident. The boat moves. The man falls into the water. The boat moves in a circle. Somebody sees the boat. The person calls for help. The lifeboat crew comes. They get a line on the boat. They stop it. Difficult words: tie up (“park” the boat), throttle (a thing which controls speed), lifeboat crew (people who help other people at sea). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 30 children were reunited with their families in Ukraine after a long operation to bring them back home from Russia where they had been taken from areas occupied by Russian forces during the war. On Friday, mothers hugged sons and daughters as they crossed the border from Belarus into Ukraine after a complex rescue mission that involved travel across four countries. Kyiv estimates that nearly 19,500 children have been taken to Russia or Russian-occupied Crimea since the country invaded Ukraine in February last year. Ukrainian officials condemned this as illegal deportation. Some children reported that they’d been separated from their parents who were pressured by Russian authorities to send their children to Russian summer camps for what was billed as two weeks. However, the children were forced to remain at the camps for four to six months, and they were moved from one place to another during their stay. Reportedly, they were closed in separate buildings and they were told that their parents no longer wanted them. Difficult words: complex (consisting of many different but related parts), condemn (to criticize), bill (to list a person or event in a program). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A rescue mission successfully reunited more than 30 children with their families in Ukraine. These children stayed in areas which Russia occupied during the war. Russian authorities sent these children to summer camps which should last two weeks. But the children had to stay there for four to six months and they often moved from place to place. They stayed in separate buildings and they got information that their families didn’t want them anymore. The children traveled across four countries before they could meet with their families again. According to Ukrainian officials, Russia illegally deported nearly 19,500 children since February last year. Difficult words: rescue mission (an operation to find and bring to safety people in a difficult situation), reunite (to come together again), deport (to make someone leave a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 30 children are back with their families in Ukraine. These children stay in areas which Russia occupies during the war with Ukraine. These children go to a summer camp. They should stay for two weeks. But they stay from four to six months. Russian authorities take the children away. They keep them in separate buildings. They tell the children that their families do not want them anymore. A special rescue mission brings the children home. The children travel across four different countries. Ukrainian officials say that Russia deports about 19,500 Ukrainian children. Difficult words: separate (without contact with each other), rescue mission (an operation in which people find someone and bring him or her back to a safe place), deport (to make someone leave a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Holy Thursday, also known as Maundy Thursday is marked uniquely by some male catholic devotees in the Philippines. They participate in a painful ritual of self-flagellation to honor the suffering that Jesus felt on the cross. Worshipers walk through the streets while beating themselves with chains and whips. As they lay on the ground in prayer, other participants hit them with wooden paddles. They believe that this painful practice will help them atone for their sins and allow them to ask for favors from God. However, some people criticize this practice as an outdated and harmful tradition. The Church itself discourages it, viewing the act of self-inflicted pain as unnecessary, since Christ has already paid for our sins. Moreover, self-harm could be a sign of deeper psychological issues and may perpetuate a cycle of trauma. Despite this, for many Filipino Catholics, it remains an integral part of their religious identity. Difficult words: devotee (a strong believer in a particular religion), self-flagellation (hitting yourself with a whip as a way to punishment), atone (to do something that shows that you are sorry for something bad that you did), self-inflicted (an injury or problem caused by your own actions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Holy Thursday, also known as Maundy Thursday, is a very unusual celebration for some male Catholics in the Philippines. Worshipers walk through the streets and they beat themselves with chains and whips. Other participants hit them with wooden sticks while they lay on the ground and pray. The men believe that God will forgive them after this painful ritual . Some people criticize the ritual as old and painful, and it can have a bad impact on a person’s mental health. The Church also said that it wasn’t necessary to suffer because Christ already suffered for people. But for many Filipino Catholics, the ritual is a part of who they are. Difficult words: worshiper (a person who takes part in a religious ceremony), ritual (a ceremony), suffer (to experience something bad or unpleasant). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Holy Thursday is a special day for Catholics in the Philippines. Some men celebrate this day in a special way. The men take part in a ritual . They wear black or red cloth. They walk through the streets and beat themselves. They use chains and whips. They lay on the ground. Others hit them with wooden sticks. The men believe that God will forgive them their sins . Some people say that this ritual is too old and painful . But for many Filipino Catholics, it is a part of who they are. Difficult words: ritual (a special way of doing or celebrating something), sin (when someone breaks a religious rule), painful (something what hurts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least four children were killed after a man armed with a small axe attacked a preschool in the city of Blumenau in southern Brazil. Police allege that the 25-year-old man gained access to the private school by scaling its walls. He turned himself in to the police after the rampage . The attacker had a history of violence and drugs, and according to police, he stabbed his grandfather in March 2021. Community members living near the school came to lay flowers and pay their respects to the young victims. In a Twitter post, President Luiz Inacio da Silva said that such a tragedy was unacceptable and an absurd act of violence against innocent and defenseless children. The attack comes a week after a 13-year-old student stabbed a teacher to death and wounded five others in Sao Paulo. Difficult words: scale (to climb up or over), rampage (violent and uncontrollable behavior), absurd (illogical and unreasonable). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man killed four children in a private preschool in southern Brazil. The 25-year-old man climbed over a wall and got inside the building. He killed four children with a small axe and injured six others. After the attack, he turned himself into the police who arrested him. Police said that in 2021, the man stabbed his grandfather, and he also had a history of violence and drugs. The attack shocked local people who came to lay flowers and pay respect to the children who died. One week ago, a 13-year-old student killed a teacher with a knife and injured five other people in Sao Paulo. Difficult words: axe (a tool used for chopping wood), stab (to attack with a knife), violence (when someone behaves badly to others and wants to hurt them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man kills four small children in a private preschool. The attack happens in southern Brazil. The man is 25 years old. He climbs over a wall. He gets inside the building. He attacks the children with an axe . He goes to the police after the attack. Police arrest him. Police say that the man attacks his grandfather with a knife in 2021. He also has problems with violence and drugs. Local people do not understand how the attack can happen. They lay flowers in front of the school. One week ago, a 13-year-old boy kills a teacher with a knife. She hurts five other people. The attack happens in Sao Paulo. Difficult words: axe (a tool which people use to chop wood), violence (when someone hurts others), lay (to put on the ground or floor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Parisians voted in favor of banning rental electric scooters from the city in a non-binding referendum. The referendum was called in response to a rising number of people being injured and killed on e-scooters in the French capital. Almost 90% of votes cast on Sunday favored a ban on the battery-powered devices; however, only under 8% of those eligible turned out to vote. Most people believe that e-scooters are accident-prone for both the users and pedestrians. However, some claimed that e-scooters were the only way to see their grandchildren who lived on the other end of the city because metros and busses didn’t work well. E-scooters have operated in the city since 2018, and Paris was one of the first cities to adopt them. But critics argue they were causing more harm than good. There was a concern with the way some people were driving the scooters. Riders often didn’t wear helmets, weaved through traffic, dodged pedestrians on pavements and got up to speeds of 27 kilometers per hour. Children as young as 12 can legally hire the e-scooters in Paris. Difficult words: non-binding (having no legal power), accident-prone (tending to be involved in a greater than average number of accidents), dodge (to avoid someone or something by a sudden quick movement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2018, Paris became one of the first cities to introduce e-scooters. But some people say that the scooters do more harm than good. Critics of the battery-powered vehicles say that they get involved in many accidents. Riders often go at high speed, they move through traffic and often they don’t wear helmets. In Paris, children as young as 12 can legally hire the scooter through a phone app. The rising number of accidents which involved e-scooters led to a referendum on banning e-scooters. The referendum took place last week and 90% of voters voted against the scooters. But only 8% of eligible voters voted, which means that the referendum has no legal power. It is up to officials how they will deal with the result. Difficult words: involve (to have something as a part), referendum (a vote in which all the people in a country or area give their opinion on something), eligible (when someone has the right to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2018, people in Paris, France, start using e-scooters. Paris is one of the first cities which has e-scooters. Three companies operate e-scooters in Paris. E-scooters have a battery for power. They can go at 27 kilometers per hour. Users can hire them through a phone app. But the number of accidents which involve e-scooters is growing. Some riders do not wear a helmet. They ride among cars. They leave the scooters in parks or on roads. A referendum takes place last week. 90% of people vote against e-scooters. They say that e-scooters are dangerous. But the result has no legal power. Only 8% of all voters come and vote. Officials can decide themselves what to do. Difficult words: operate (to make something work or be in action), hire (to pay money to be able to use something), referendum (a vote in which all the people in a country or area give their opinion on something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Tuesday, Finland formally joined the NATO military alliance, and it became the 31st member of the North Atlantic Treaty. The historic policy shift brought on by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine quickly drew a threat from Moscow. Russian President Vladimir Putin had cited opposing NATO expansion as one justification for his invasion. Finnish officials said joining NATO would make the country safer and NATO stronger, and that the next goal was to get Finland’s good neighbor Sweden to the full membership. Finland’s accession roughly doubles the length of the border that NATO shares with Russia and bolsters its eastern flank. The NATO Collective Defense Pact states that an attack on one member is an attack on all. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 prompted Finns to seek security under NATO, ending the military non-alignment it has maintained since 1945. On Monday, Russia said that the move raised the prospect of conflict in Ukraine and that the country would strengthen its military capacity in its Western and Northwestern regions. NATO has repeatedly stressed it’s solely a defensive alliance and doesn’t threaten Russia. Difficult words: justification (a good reason or explanation for something), bolster (to support or strengthen), non-alignment (not supporting or depending on any powerful country or group of countries). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since 1945, Finland wasn’t part of any alliance , but when Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, the country changed its policy . Since February last year, Finland wanted to join NATO to be protected from possible attacks from Russia. The NATO Collective Defense Pact says that if an attack on one NATO member happens, it is an attack on all. On Tuesday, Finland joined NATO, which almost doubled NATO’s border with Russia. Finnish officials said that joining NATO would make the country safer. They also said that they wanted their good neighbor Sweden to join the military alliance, too. In a reaction, Russia said that it would increase its military activity in the northwest and that the fact that Finland joined NATO could escalate the conflict in Ukraine. Difficult words: alliance (a group of countries who work together), policy (a set of ideas or plans), escalate (to increase). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Tuesday, Finland becomes a member of NATO. NATO is a military alliance . 31 countries are in NATO. If someone attacks one member of NATO, it is an attack on all. When Russia attacks Ukraine in February 2022, Finland does not feel safe. Finland is Russia’s neighbor. Finland worries that Russia can attack it, too. When Finland joins NATO, NATO’s border with Russia doubles . Now, Finland wants Sweden to join NATO, too. Sweden is a good neighbor of Finland. Russia’s reaction is not good. Russian officials say that they will bring more soldiers to the country’s northwestern border . It can also make the war in Ukraine worse. Difficult words: military alliance (a group of countries who fight together in a war), double (to become twice as much or many), border (the line between two countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An American family called for help after its 10-kilogram Himalayan cat scratched its seven-month-old baby and held all of them hostage inside a bedroom. The conversation between the family and emergency services was recorded. The victims said that their cat had a history of violence and was being really bad at that moment. Luckily, the baby did not need any medical attention. Emergency services sent the police over to contain the cat, and the family is considering what to do with its feline foe now that there is a baby. Difficult words: feline (a cat), foe (an enemy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Something unusual happened to an American family. Their seven-month-old baby was attacked by the family’s cat. Luckily, the baby was not seriously injured. It only had some scratches on its forehead. However, the family was trapped in the bedroom for some time, as the cat wouldn’t let them out. The cat is a large Himalayan . It weighs 22 pounds (10 kilograms) and it has a history of violence . The family didn’t know what to do, so the man called the police, and the cat was contained . The family is now considering what to do with the cat. Difficult words: Himalayan (a very large pet cat), violence (attacking and hurting somebody), contain (stop or control), consider (think about). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An American family has a big cat. It is 22 pounds (10 kilograms) heavy. The family has a baby, too. It is seven months old. The cat attacks the baby. The baby is not injured badly. Its head is only a little scratched . However , the family has a problem. They are in the bedroom. The cat is outside the room. The family cannot get out of the bedroom. If they get out, the cat attacks them. The man calls the police. The police come and stop the cat. Difficult words: injured (have problems with the body), scratch (to cut skin a little), however (but). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists mounted a camera on a falcon’s back to study the physics of flight while the birds are hunting. The videos revealed that the birds use a kind of “motion camouflaging ”, as they zigzag , trying to catch their next dinner. The predators also use their wide field of vision to keep their eyes firmly fixed on their prey while they move in the air. Difficult words: mounted (fixed), camouflaging (hiding), predator (an animal which hunts other animals), prey (an animal which is killed and eaten by another animal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A great video, which was taken in Belgium in 2011, emerged. It was taken by a camera which was fixed on a falcon ’s back. Scientists used the video to study falcons. The scientists were interested in the physics of flight while the birds hunt. The video revealed to scientists that the birds use a kind of “motion camouflaging ”, as they fly to catch their dinner. The birds also use their wide field of vision to keep their eyes fixed on their prey . Difficult words: falcon (a big bird which catches smaller birds), camouflage (hide), prey (an animal which is killed and eaten by another animal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists study birds. They want to know how they fly. They put a camera on a bird. This type of bird hunts smaller birds. It catches them in the air. The camera films this. Scientists learn from the video. The bird’s flight is special. The bird can see very well. This helps the bird to catch small birds. Difficult words: scientist (clever person who is an expert in something), hunt (catch and eat), flight (flying). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Footage captured the moment climate activists poured a black liquid into a 17th-century Barcaccia fountain in Rome, Italy. The activists from the Last Generation group ‘Ultima Generaziona’ said they had chosen a fountain to highlight the dangers that global warming poses to water supply and sea levels. They dyed the famous Spanish Steps fountain black with a vegetable-based liquid to protest against climate change inaction. In a tweet, the group said that it was absurd that such a gesture should shock people when the world was experiencing a drought emergency that was putting agriculture and energy production in crisis. The three men and a woman were removed by the police, put into custody, and they are facing charges of defacing a public monument and entering the fountain. Rome’s mayor Roberto Gualtieri visited the fountain designed by Pietro Bernini in 1629, and he said that Rome was at the forefront of the fight against climate change and the protection of the artistic heritage. Difficult words: absurd (unreasonable or illogical), deface (to spoil the surface of something, for example by drawing or writing on it), at the forefront (in a leading position). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On April 1, activists from the Last Generation group poured a black liquid into a fountain in Rome, Italy. Pietro Bernini designed the Barcaccia fountain in 1629. The fountain is at the base of the Spanish Steps in central Rome, and it is one of the most visited sites in Rome. Three men and one woman stepped into the fountain and opened bags with a black powder, which turned the water black. The police arrested the people and put them into custody. The group wrote on social media that such a gesture shocked people, but they didn’t care that the world was experiencing a drought emergency. The activists wanted to make people notice that global warming is impacting water supply and sea levels, and that world leaders don’t do enough to solve this problem. Difficult words: pour (to send something flowing or falling), gesture (an action to express an idea), drought (a long period without or with little rain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Last Generation is a group of climate activists. They take action to protect the natural world. Last weekend, three men and one woman step into a famous fountain in Rome, Italy. The Barcaccia fountain is from the 17 th century. It is at the bottom of the famous Spanish Steps. Thousands of tourists come here every day. The activists pour black liquid into the fountain. The water turns black. On social media, the activists say that changing weather has a bad impact on water in the world. It rains a little. Farmers do not have enough water to grow crops . Sea levels are rising. World leaders and people do not care about these problems. Black water in a fountain is more shocking for them. The police arrest the activists. They are in custody now. Difficult words: crop (a plant which grows in the field), sea level (where the sea meets the land), shocking (very bad or unpleasant). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New York-based artist Kris Kashtanova created an 18-page comic book ‘Zarya of the Dawn’ with the help of the AI program Midjourney. She received a copyright for the comic in September 2022 but five months later, the US Copyright Office reversed itself saying the images in Zarya weren’t the product of human authorship . The case has ignited the debate about who owns AI-generated artwork and whether artwork needs to be created by a human being. Intellectual property and copyright are ways how people control and profit from creativity. Anyone who engages in creative expression usually has immediate legal rights to it; however, courts have long held that the author has to be a human being and that AI tools so far don’t demonstrate the necessary amount of originality and human work. Artists and companies that own creative content oppose copyright protection for AI artwork saying that the algorithms work by training themselves on vast quantities of material on the open web, some of which is already copyrighted. Difficult words: copyright (the legal right to print, publish, perform, or record an artistic material), authorship (when someone is the person who wrote a particular book article, play, and so on), intellectual property (creations of human intellect). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

AI programs transform the art world, but the legal system doesn’t know yet who owns the creative output — the users, the owners of the programs, or maybe no one at all. US artist Krish Karhtanova created a comic book with the help of an AI program. In September 2022, she received a copyright from the US Copyright Office, but five months later, the office reversed itself. The office said that there was no human author of the book, and only humans could receive the copyright. People who create art usually have the legal right to print, publish or sell it. But experts don’t know how to solve situations when people use AI to create art. AI programs usually use free materials on the internet to create new things. But these materials are usually already subject to copyright. Difficult words: output (something produced by a person, machine, or industry), copyright (the legal right to print, publish or sell an artistic material), reverse ((to take back one’s decision). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People, who create art, get a copyright from a copyright office. Copyright means that an artist can officially print, publish or sell his or her art. These days, some artists use AI programs to create art. Experts cannot decide who owns the copyright in such situation. One US artist makes a comic book. AI program helps her. This woman gets a copyright from the US Copyright Office. But five months later, the office says that the author of the book is not a human . So the artist cannot have the copyright. Legal experts do not know who owns AI-generated art. If it is the author, the user, or the owner of the program. Some people also argue that AI programs use materials from the internet, and these materials have a copyright. Difficult words: human (connected to people), legal expert (a person who understands law), AI-generated (something what is created by a computer which performs people’s tasks). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Located in the Old City of Jerusalem, The Western Wall is the most religious site in the world for the Jewish people who come to pray for the unity of the people of Israel. Thousands of people of all faiths journey to the wall every year to visit and recite prayers. Traditionally, these prayers are either spoken or written down and placed in the cracks of the wall. The wall splits into two sections, one area for males and the other for females. Last week, a team of men equipped with long wooden sticks or only with their hands removed written prayers that visitors to the Western Wall in Jerusalem traditionally cram into its crevices . The notes to God are then buried on Jerusalem’s Mount of Olives, in accordance with ritual. This happens every year on the eve of Passover, one of the Jewish religion’s most sacred and widely observed holidays. In Judaism, Passover commemorates the story of the Israelites’ departure from ancient Egypt that appears in the Hebrew Bible books of Exodus, Numbers, and other texts. The men clear the notes in order to allow people room to place new notes. This year, there have been many more notes and there have been many visitors to the Western Wall in the past three months. Difficult words: crevice (a narrow opening in a rock or wall), in accordance (in a way that follows a rule or request), commemorate (to keep alive the memory of an event by a ceremony). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Western Wall is in the Old City of Jerusalem, Israel, and for the Jewish people, it is the most sacred place in the world. Thousands of people come to the wall to pray , and some put written prayers in the wall’s cracks. These prayers are notes to God, and most people pray for the unity of the people of Israel. Last week, a team of men cleared the cracks to make place for new notes. They used long wooden sticks or only their hands. The tradition is to bury these notes on Jerusalem’s Mount of Olives. It happens every year on the evening of Passover, the most important holiday for Jewish people. They remember the story of how the Israelites left Egypt. Difficult words: sacred (connected with God), pray (to speak to a god), unity (being together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Western Wall is in Jerusalem, Israel. For Jewish people, the wall is the most important place in the world. Every year, thousands of people come to the wall. They pray . Some people write prayers on a small piece of paper. They put this paper in the cracks of the wall. Most people pray for the unity of people of Israel. This year, even more people come than in the past. Passover is the most important holiday for Jewish people. They remember the story of Israelites who leave Egypt in the past. On the evening of Passover, a team of men clear the notes from the wall. They use long sticks or only their hands. They then bury the notes on the Mount of Olives. Difficult words: pray (to speak to a god), unity (being together), bury (to put underground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Soaring inflation is taking the stream out of Hungary’s wedding market, supercharged in recent years by Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s lavish family support measures. The number of weddings plunged to a nine-year low at the start of 2023. Couples reported that they exceeded their wedding budget several times and they had to make uneasy compromises. The government’s measures have fueled a wedding boom in recent years and lifted Hungary to the top of the EU matrimony table. However, Hungary is projected to run the EU’s highest average inflation rate at 16.4% this year. This has led to the number of guests at weddings dramatically decreasing. Twenty years ago, the average wedding had 100 to 120 guests, then 10 years ago, it was 80 to 100, and now, weddings with 60 guests are the most frequent. This shows that couples don’t have enough money to throw a really big party. Difficult words: supercharge (to make something faster or more powerful), lavish (generous and impressive with a lot of money spent on), matrimony (the state of being married). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s family support caused a boom in weddings in recent years. But now, the situation on the wedding market in Hungary is changing. With 16.4%, Hungary had the highest inflation in the EU, which caused prices of many things to go up dramatically. Many couples said that they exceeded the wedding budget several times, and often they had to look for cheaper things than they wanted to have. Also, the number of guests at a wedding went down. Twenty years ago, it was usual to have 100 to 120 guests at a wedding, but these days, the average wedding has 60 guests. Difficult words: boom (the time when something is popular), inflation (the price of money), budget (the amount of money a person can spend on something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Twenty years ago, Hungarian weddings usually have 100 to 120 guests. Now, there are normally 60 guests at a wedding. Viktor Orban is Hungary’s Prime Minister. He makes laws which help young people and families. It means that more people are getting married. But the situation is very different in 2023. Hungary has the highest inflation in the EU. The inflation is 16.4%. It means that everything is very expensive. Young people have a budget for their weddings. But the money is not usually enough. They spend several times more money than they want. They often choose cheaper things than they want. Difficult words: wedding (a ceremony when two people get married), inflation (the price of money), budget (the amount of money which a person can spend on something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gabon’s home to one of the world’s largest intact rainforests. However, in today’s financial markets, its trees are worth more dead than alive. The country wants to cash in on its efforts by selling carbon credits . The forests of Gabon absorb and store millions of tons of carbon dioxide every year. For the past decade, the country has carefully protected them, but now, its oil revenue is dwindling and the government’s looking for ways to maximize its revenue from the trees. The multi-pronged Grande Mayumba project will operate in logging, cattle farming, and ecotourism. The high-end safari lodge will cost 2,000 dollars a night, and it’ll be one of the few places left on earth where one can see gorillas, leopards, elephants, and buffaloes and where hippos walk out from the forest directly onto the beach. A joint venture with an Italian company sustainably harvests woods in Gabon, which means harvesting without exhausting the forest’s resources and enabling it to regenerate. The local community has raised concerns over Grande Mayumba ahead of this year’s presidential election. They worry that restrictions on land could mean that residents can no longer fish, hunt or grow sustainable crops. Difficult words: cash in (to take advantage of a situation), carbon credit (a permit that allows the owner to emit a certain amount of carbon dioxide or other greenhouse gases), dwindle (to decrease gradually), high-end (of very good quality and usually expensive). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Gabon is one of the last places in the world where you can see gorillas, leopards, elephants, or hippos. Gabon’s forests are the largest in the world and they are still intact . The country’s profit from oil went down in recent years and the government is looking for new ways how to make money without destroying the forest. A new project called Grande Mayumbe aims to get money from logging , farming, and ecotourism . Workers are building safari houses which will cost 2,000 dollars per night and up to 20 people can stay there at the same time. An Italian company is logging trees sustainably, which means that it cuts down just enough trees for the forest to regenerate. Local people worry that the project will have a negative impact on their lives and that they will no longer be able to fish, hunt or grow crops. Difficult words: intact (complete and in the original state), logging (cutting down trees for their wood), ecotourism (holidays to places of natural beauty in a way which helps local people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gabon is a special place. It is one of the last places in the world where you can see gorillas, leopards, or elephants. The largest forests are in Gabon. They are intact. It means that people don’t destroy them. But the country has problems with money. In the past, Gabon gets a lot of money from oil. Now, there is not so much oil anymore. The government is looking for new ways to make money. One possibility is ecotourism . Workers are building a safari with small houses. Tourists can live there. It costs 2,000 dollars per night. Another possibility to make money is logging . But companies can cut down only a limited number of trees. It is important that the forest can regenerate . Some people worry that new businesses will have a bad impact on their lives. They are afraid that they will not be able to fish, hunt and grow plants for food. Difficult words: ecotourism (holidays to places of natural beauty in a way which helps local people), logging (cutting down trees for their wood), regenerate (to grow again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Saturday, the Russian president Vladimir Putin said, that he would station tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, Ukraine’s neighbor. It’s one of Russia’s most pronounced nuclear signals since the beginning of its invasion of Ukraine 13 months ago. Putin likened it to the US stationing its weapons in Europe, while insisting that Russia wouldn’t violate its nuclear non- proliferation promises. NATO spokesperson said that Russia had consistently broken its arms control commitments and that Putin’s rhetoric was dangerous and irresponsible. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry called for an extraordinary meeting of the UN Security Council and for the international community to take decisive measures to prevent Russia’s use of nuclear weapons. Difficult words: liken (to compare), proliferation (increasing the number or amount of something), rhetoric (the technique of using language effectively). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Saturday, the Russian president Vladimir Putin said, that he would place nuclear weapons in Belarus, Ukraine’s neighbor. Putin said that placing weapons in Belarus was the same as the US placing nuclear weapons in Europe. At the same time, he said that Russia wouldn’t increase the number of nuclear weapons. NATO’s spokesperson said that Putin’s words were dangerous and irresponsible and that he repeatedly broke his promises. Ukraine’s officials called for a meeting of the UN Security Council and asked the international community to take steps to stop Russia from using nuclear weapons. Difficult words: irresponsible (not thinking carefully enough or not caring about the result of an action), repeatedly (again and again), international community (the countries of the world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Saturday, the Russian President Vladimir Putin says, that he will place nuclear weapons in Belarus. Belarus is Ukraine’s neighbor. Putin says that the US has nuclear weapons in Europe. It is the same thing. But Putin also says that Russia will not increase the number of nuclear weapons. Many countries do not believe it. NATO’s spokesperson says that Putin’s words are dangerous. Putin breaks his promises in the past. Ukraine’s officials want a meeting of the UN Security Council. They say that countries of the world must stop Putin from using nuclear weapons. Difficult words: nuclear weapon (a bomb or rocket which uses dangerous nuclear energy which comes from breaking small things called atoms), increase (to make something greater or bigger), promise (when someone says that he will or will not do something in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

One police and a protester were seriously injured in clashes during an unauthorized demonstration against the construction of a reservoir for farm irrigation in Western France. At least 6,000 protesters joined the march and they threw fireworks and other projectiles at the police as they crossed fields to approach the construction area. France’s worst drought on record last summer sharpened the debate over water resources in the European Union’s biggest agricultural sector. Supporters said that artificial reservoirs were a way to use water efficiently when needed. However, critics called the reservoirs mega basins that were outsized and favored large farms. The irrigation project protest comes after weeks of anti-pension reform demonstrations that have turned violent. The French government pushed through the legislation without a final parliamentary vote. Difficult words: unauthorized (not having official permission or approval), irrigation (the supply of water to land or crops), outsized (exceptionally large). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, more than 6,000 people protested in Western France. But authorities didn’t allow the demonstration. People protested against building a reservoir for farm irrigation . They said that the reservoir was far too big and only big farms would benefit from it. Authorities, on the other hand, said that the reservoir was necessary because of the changing weather. Last summer in France was the hottest in history. The reservoir would hold water and farmers could use it in times of drought . Many protests are taking place in France right now. A few weeks ago, the French government approved a pension reform, which started a wave of violent protests in many cities across the country. Difficult words: irrigation (bringing water to land and fields), benefit (to have a good or helpful result of effect), drought (a long period with little or no rain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last summer in France is the hottest in history. Officials look for ways how to help farmers grow crops. There is a plan to build a water reservoir in Western France. Farmers can use water from this reservoir when it does not rain. They bring the water to their fields. But many people protest against the reservoir. They say that the reservoir is too big. They worry that only big farms will have water from it. 6,000 people protest last week. But authorities do not allow the protest. Big protests are in France now. The government passes a new law about pensions . Many people are angry. Difficult words: reservoir (a big tank), allow (to let something happen), pension (money which the government pays to a person who does not work anymore). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Australian lawmaker, Jeremy Buckingham, set Queensland’s Condamine River on fire to show the impact of the coal seam gas industry and fracking operations nearby. In the video, you can see the MP putting a lighter to the river, which ignites a huge flame. After recovering from the shock, Buckingham says a few words about what has occurred, advocating for a stop to the drilling of methane gas just a kilometer away. Difficult words: impact (an effect), coal seam gas (a type of gas which is mostly the methane gas), fracking (putting a liquid in the ground to make gas or oil come out), MP (a member of parliament), ignite (start), huge (very big), advocate (speak for or against something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An Australian member of parliament was on a boat in a river. He then put a lighter in the river and set it on fire! Someone filmed everything. The river is in Queensland and there is a fracking site just a kilometer away. Methane is coming up and that is what was on fire. The lawmaker wants to put a stop to this. Difficult words: fracking (putting something in the ground to make gas or oil come out), site (area, the place where something happens), methane (a type of gas which can get on fire). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Australia. An Australian MP is on a boat in a river. He has a lighter . He puts the lighter near the river and the river gets on fire! Someone films everything. Water does not burn , but methane does. Methane is a type of gas. It is coming up the river. It is coming up because there is a fracking site . The MP wants to stop it. Difficult words: MP (a member of parliament – a government), lighter (a small thing which makes fire), burn (to be on fire), fracking (putting a machine in the ground to make gas or oil come out so you can sell it later), site (the place where something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe’s winter has come to an end; however, some countries are already preparing for the next year. Italy took a key step toward securing energy independence from Russia. The first regasification vessel arrived in the city of Piombino on the western coast of Italy last week. It’s considered crucial to secure the energy supply and to reach Italy’s energy independence from Russia. Before the invasion of Ukraine, 40% of Italy’s imported gas came from Russia. Now, Russian gas accounts for less than 10%. Without the ship that will import liquefied natural gas, the next winter could be challenging. However, local activists have staged protests, citing its potential impact on the city, fishing, and tourism. For officials, it’s essential to find a common ground between industry and citizens to ensure energy supply and survival. Difficult words: regasification vessel (a ship that transports, stores and changes liquefied gas into gas onboard), liquefied (made liquid), common ground (shared interests or opinions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Before the invasion of Ukraine, Italy imported 40% of its natural gas from Russia. Now, the country imports less than 10% of gas from Russia. But the country is already preparing for next winter, and at the same time, it wants to be completely independent of Russia. Last week, the first regasification ship arrived in the city of Piombino. This ship transports and stores gas which is made liquid. It then changes the liquefied gas into a gas again. Officials believe that this ship will help get enough gas to Italy next winter. Some local people don’t agree with the project. They say that it will have a bad impact on life in the city, on fishing and tourism. Difficult words: import (to bring things from abroad to sell), independent (when a person or thing doesn’t depend on anyone or anything else), liquefied (made liquid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Italy imports gas from Russia. Before the invasion of Ukraine, Italy imports 40% of its gas from Russia. Now, it is less than 10%. The country is already preparing for next winter. Italy wants to be independent of gas from Russia. One solution is regasification ships. The first ship arrives in the city of Piombino last week. The ship transports and stores liquefied gas. It changes the liquefied gas into a gas again. It happens on board. Some people are not happy with the ship. They say that it will have a bad impact on local life, fishing, and tourism. Difficult words: import (to bring things from another country to sell), independent (working or happening freely), local (living in a particular place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Missouri, USA, Xavier Cunningham climbed in a tree when insects attacked him, and he fell onto a meat skewer which went into his skull. It passed by major arteries in his brain, and doctors at the University of Kansas Health System were able to remove it. About 100 people worked on helping Xavier. Brain surgeons, ENT surgeons, paediatric ICU doctors, trauma doctors, and anaesthesia doctors helped him. The doctors said that his survival was ‘ miraculous ’. Difficult words: skewer (a thin, long piece of metal that people use to cook meat or vegetables), artery (a very big tube that passes blood throughout the body), ENT (ear-nose-throat), paediatric (relating to children), ICU (intensive care unit—where someone goes in a hospital when something very serious happens), miraculous (like a miracle – magical, amazing). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: skewer (a thin, long piece of metal for cooking meat or vegetables), artery (a very big tube that moves blood inside the body), miraculous (like a miracle – magical, amazing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
